transactions.buyer: Khosla family (Neeru Khosla controlling owner; Vinod Khosla chair; Neal Khosla vice chair) with co-investors incl. Mark Stevens, Penny Pritzker, Carlyle and Dynasty Equity, Sixth Street
transactions.notes: Seed figures confirmed: $9.612B for 100% of Football Northwest LLC (includes Lumen Field lease through 2032), agreed Jul 11, unanimously approved Aug 26, closed Sep 3 2026 (team release). 13.6x 2025 revenue is Sportico's figure ('just over $700M', from the Allen & Co. sales deck); revenueAtDeal is implied ($9.612B/13.6), hence isEstimated. S&P Global Market Intelligence instead puts the multiple at ~15.0x. Khosla had to divest his 3.1% 49ers stake. Financing not disclosed.

transactions.seller: Arthur Blank / Falcons (whether shares come from Blank or existing LPs not disclosed)
transactions.notes: Not among the seeds; found in sweep. $10.6B is a blended headline EV: reportedly a first tranche of 7.5% at just over $10B, with the remaining 2.5% ~18 months later at ~$11B (tranche detail from a single source). NFL vote expected in October 2026. Would be Arctos' fourth NFL stake (Bills, Chargers, Browns).

transactions.buyer: Egon Durban-led group: Egon Durban (~11%), Michael Meldman (~5.4%), Michael Dell (5.3%), Joseph Baratta (1.7%), Ari Emanuel (1.4%), Mark Shapiro (0.6%)
transactions.seller: First Football (Paul Leff, David Abrams, Dan Goldring), exiting its entire stake held since 2007
transactions.notes: $9.9B is the enterprise value; total consideration was ~$11B including the 10% relocation 'flip tax' paid to the league. The Emanuel/Shapiro stakes are part of this single 25.3% transaction, not separate deals. After closing Durban ~22%, Meldman ~12.9%. Approval 'Tuesday in Orlando' at the May spring meeting = May 19, 2026 (date inferred from meeting timing); closing was expected late May but not confirmed.

transactions.seller: Haslam Sports Group (Jimmy and Dee Haslam)
transactions.notes: Seed confirmed. First tranche (~3%; SportsPro says 3.2%) of a planned 10% across three tranches (~$900M total); Bloomberg says 'more than $9B'. Proceeds support the Brook Park stadium. 13.4x revenue multiple is S&P Global Market Intelligence's figure (seen via search snippet only). Later tranches not yet reported approved.

transactions.buyer: Egon Durban (some reports also name Michael Meldman)
transactions.notes: CORRECTED from seed (7%): the NFL approved 3.5%, with another 3.5% expected to follow later (not separately confirmed). CNBC says 'over $11 billion'; $11.1B is the most-cited figure, and it appears to include the 10% flip tax paid to the NFL, so ex-tax EV is lower (not reported). Approved alongside Davis's succession plan giving Durban a right of first refusal on control.

Seed confirmed. The 1% is in the Ross holding company: Dolphins plus Hard Rock Stadium, the F1 Miami Grand Prix and the Miami Open. So $12.5B is NOT a team-only valuation. Approved by the NFL Mar 31, 2026; the team said closing was expected within days (not confirmed).

Seed confirmed; Oct 2025 is the approval date, and Bloomberg first reported the deal Sep 3, 2025. Initial reports said ~$10B. $10.3B at approval (CNBC) is the most cited; a Sportico summary said 'just over $10.5B'. Unanimous approval at the fall meeting.

transactions.seller: Kraft family (new equity; proceeds stay on the team balance sheet)
transactions.notes: CORRECTED dates vs seed 'Nov 2025': announced Sep 25, approved Oct 22, reported closed Nov 11, 2025 (closing date from a single source). $9B is pre-money; Sportico gives $9.7B post-money. Proceeds (~$720M) are primary capital. Excludes the New England Revolution. This was Sixth Street's first NFL deal.

transactions.buyer: Pete Briger Jr. (Fortress Investment Group) and family
transactions.notes: Second 2025 49ers LP sale (not a seed item). About $272–275M for 3.2%, valuation reported as $8.5–8.6B. Approved at the Oct 2025 fall meeting with the Giants and Patriots deals. York family retains ~85%.

Seed confirmed (2.3–2.35%). Existing owners bought out an estate's stake, so this is a consolidation with no new investor. First reported in August at $8.8B (Sportico/Bloomberg); $8.9B at approval (CNBC/Sun-Times) is the most cited. Reported finalized late Sep 2025.

transactions.buyer: Khosla family (3.1%), Deeter family (2.1%), Griffith family (1%)
transactions.notes: Valuation reported as 'over $8.5B' at announcement and $8.6B at approval (~$533M for 6.2%). Khosla's 3.1% had to be divested in 2026 as a condition of the Seahawks purchase; the buyer of that stake is not reported.
Valuation not disclosed. Sportico's 2025 NFL team values says 'north of $6 billion', a single source and only a floor, so it is left null (see unverified). Arctos' second NFL stake after the Bills.

transactions.buyer: Josh Harris-led group (with Mitchell Rales, Magic Johnson, ~20 LPs)
transactions.notes: Reference comp outside the 2025+ scope. Exclusive agreement May 12, 2023; approved Jul 20, 2023; closed shortly after. Price reportedly includes a ~$250M earn-out. The NFL capped acquisition debt at $1.1B, but actual debt used was not disclosed, so amountFinanced is null. The ~11x revenue multiple is cited in Sportico's 2026 Seahawks coverage.
